newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises 5.55 bln stg in March - BBA.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises 5.55 bln stg in March - BBA.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banking groups to the private sector rose a seasonally adjusted 5.551 billion stg in March, the largest monthly increase since 1991, the British Bankers Association said on Friday.
The jump in lending was well above February's 3.345 billion stg increase and the underlying six monthly average increase of 2.5 billion stg.
But last month's figure included some 1.7 billion pounds of lending through reverse repos.

"Major banks' lending rose by...the largest monthly increase since the series began in 1991," said BBA director-general Tim Sweeney. "Much of the rise was to financial companies and included a sizeable amount of lending by way of reverse repos."

Consumer credit rose by 298 million pounds in March, including an extra 115 million in credit card lending -- substantially below February's record 594 million stg increase and the recent monthly average rise of 433 million.
Lending to the financial sector rose "very strongly", by 1.749 billion stg -- also the highest underlying increase since the series started.
Individuals increased their borrowing by 1.041 billion stg in March, down from February's record 1.367 billion rise.
Mortgage lending rose by 755 million stg last month, just below February's 780 million increase but comfortably above the monthly average of 689 million.
Lending to the manufacturing sector was virtually flat, the BBA said.
"While mortgage lending remained above the recent monthly average in March, the rise in consumer credit was noticeably more muted than of late," Sweeney said.
"To complete the picture, there was a modest rise in lending to industry and commerce."
